title: Throughput telemetry orchestrator and customer acceptance protocol
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a composable load-testing harness + benchmarking methodology and a repeatable customer acceptance protocol for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. This ticket delivers the orchestration layer (telemetry-orchestrator), test profiles, grading rubric, and onboarding checklist used during Dedicated customer onboarding and SLA verification.

Scope and components:
- Telemetry Orchestrator (TO): a lightweight controller service that spins up test agents, schedules tenant-mix scenarios, injects jitter and client-side concurrency patterns, and collects end-to-end traces and resource metrics. The TO will be implemented as a Python CLI that calls existing prober binaries and the fleet test API.
- Scenario library: canonical scenarios (steady sustained, ramp+burst, mixed-tenancy, cold-KV-cache, long-context sessions) with parameterized knobs for QPS, request size, seq-length distribution, and tenant weight.
- Fidelity shim: a translator that maps customer request distributions from shadow replay traces into the scenario library (preserves request size, prompt templates, and KV cache hit curves).
- Observability and grading: Grafana dashboards and a grading script that produces a pass/fail report with the following metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, GPU utilization, memory pressure, tail-latency SLO breaches, error rate, and headroom margin (throughput at 95% utilization).
- Acceptance protocol: a checklist and signing flow for customer sign-off that includes in-lab validation, optional on-customer-replay, and an operational runbook for failed validations (fallback model, increased reserved capacity, or tuning guidance).

Acceptance criteria (must be met for Done):
1) Telemetry Orchestrator CLI can run any scenario from the scenario library and emit standard JSON summaries and traces to S3 and to the telemetry pipeline.
2) Grading script produces deterministic pass/fail based on configurable thresholds (default: p99 latency < 400ms, error rate < 0.5%, GPU util < 95% sustained).
3) At least three canonical scenarios validated on staging fleet identical to production with reproducible artifacts (dashboard snapshots, JSON grade reports, and run logs) stored in the dedicated-throughput artifacts folder.
4) Customer acceptance checklist drafted and reviewed by Solutions Eng, Product, and SRE.
5) Runbook created for common failure modes (high tail, KV-cache warmup issues, noisy tenants) with mitigation steps and rollback guidance.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing a full-scale replay engine (we will integrate customer replay via the fidelity shim and existing replay drivers).
- Not changing autoscaler logic yet — this ticket focuses on measurement and acceptance, autoscaler changes will be follow-ups.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive is the headroom margin? We propose a default 5% buffer for on-prem and 10% for shared Dedicated pools; Ops asked for configurable per-customer margins.
- Synthetic vs replay balance: full customer replay is highest fidelity but expensive; decide when to require replay vs scenario-based verification.
- Storage and retention for artifacts: default 90 days for grade reports, 365 days for customer-signed acceptance artifacts.

Links to artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/DEDICATED-Throughput+Orchestrator (draft)
- GitHub prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probers/pull/219 (prototype TO CLI)
- Dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/orchestrator-template

Next milestones:
- 2026-03-06: deliver prototype TO that can run steady sustained and ramp scenarios (INTERNAL DEMO).
- 2026-03-12: grading script and dashboard snapshot generation (current).
- 2026-03-18: staging validation of three canonical scenarios and first customer-facing acceptance checklist.

Notes on measurement methodology:
- Use distributed clients across AZs to avoid client-side saturation artifacts.
- Inject realistic inter-request jitter (based on production percentiles) to surface concurrency-sensitive bottlenecks.
- Warming phase: each test must include a warmup window sized to the model's KV-cache characteristics (configurable, defaults: 3x median session length).
- Tail capture: include per-request trace IDs to correlate server-side span durations and GPU kernel timing, enabling attribution of tail events to model architecture vs infra noise.

acceptance_criteria: TO CLI runs scenario and exports JSON summary to configured storage
Grading script produces deterministic pass/fail with default thresholds and outputs a signed PDF for customer sign-off
Three canonical scenarios validated on staging with dashboards and artifacts
Customer acceptance checklist reviewed by Solutions Eng, Product, and SRE
Runbook for common failure modes documented and reviewed
runbook_items: If p99 > threshold during sustained test: switch to conservative model variant and re-run scenario
If GPU util > 98% and tail increases: recommend increasing reserved capacity or enabling quantized variant
If KV-cache cold starts cause spikes: enforce longer warmup window and document expected warmup profile
If noisy tenant detected: isolate tenant and re-run single-tenant validation, escalate to tenant QoS policy team
